transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Kievone.
European Union negotiators are deeply disappointed with the collapse of climate talks in Turkey.
Terry Schultz reports the EU team said it could not accept the final draft that omitted
the mention of fossil fuel, considered one of the main drivers of environmental damage.
Despite record-long and extended negotiations to reach a compromise, Irish Environment Minister
Dara O'Brien, negotiating on behalf of the EU, said the absence of any mention of transitioning
away from coal, oil and gas was a disgrace.
We could not, with any good conscience, support a text that effectively denies what is happening
in the world and was hijacked by fossil fuel producers.
O'Brien's fellow negotiator, EU Climate Commissioner Whoopke Hoekstra, echoed the disappointment.
This is larger than just all of us.
This is something that doesn't discriminate and that humanity urgently needs to tackle.
Hoekstra said the EU will continue working with like-minded countries and redouble its
own efforts to combat climate change.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
A leaked intelligence memo says the Pentagon is putting new limits on military cooperation
with Canada.
The Canadian Defence Minister says the two militaries are still working closely together.
Julian Abraham has details.
The leaked Classified Department of Defence memo, first reported by The Washington Post,
has dominated conversations at the Halifax International Security Forum.
Republican South Dakota Senator Mike Rounds confirmed its existence in a speech at the
forum.
While it was a classified discussion, it was one that was put together several months ago,
only recently signed, and then it was unfortunately then released publicly.
Rounds says, according to the memo, U.S. military officials will need permission to attend Canadian
think-tank events or social gatherings, the latest strain on an already fraught relationship
between the two allies.
But speaking at the forum, Canada's Defence Minister David McGinty insisted cooperation
with the U.S. on defence, security and intelligence continues.
For NPR News, I'm Julian Abraham in Halifax.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson is condemning the arrest of two people as they boarded an
Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport yesterday.
He says he did speak to the airline.
I made my view very clear to Alaska Airlines, they need to call on ICE to get out of our
airports.
Reacting to the arrest video.
The video is horrific and it is chilling.
Masked agents who do not identify themselves during screaming individuals off a jetway
as they're about to do something very ordinary in our country, bored of flight.
Homeland Security says the operation targeted a man who overstayed his visa and alleges
that a woman threw hot coffee at officers.
Alaska Airlines says it has no advance notice and is reviewing whether proper procedures
were followed.
The Port of Seattle says it is in talks with Homeland Security.
This is NPR News in Washington.
The new Democratic-controlled Congress that convenes in January today hit a milestone
of at least 258 seats, with confirmation that Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican
Virginia Fox in North Carolina.
Four other House races remain outstanding, two of which are in Louisiana and are heading
to a December runoff.
A sweep like this for House seats has not been seen since 1992.
Researchers are developing brain implants that can help restore people's speech and
movement, and PR's Ping Wong has more.
A 58-year-old trained singer had lost much of her ability to speak and sing due to ALS,
a disease that destroys nerve cells that control muscle movement.
Maitreyi Wairakar is a neuroscientist at UC Davis.
She and her colleagues designed an implant that connects to parts of the singer's brain
related to speech, pitch, and tone.
We designed a task to enable her to sing a musical scale.
We asked her to sing a typical major scale, and we were able to decode all the notes that
she sang with very high accuracy.
The implant records her brain signals into a computer, which translates them into commands.
The technology is still largely experimental and was presented at the Society for Neuroscience
conference.
Ping Wong, NPR News.
Heavy rain that started in Florida is forecast to move north, saturating parts of New England
through Monday, early this week's snow is expected in parts of Michigan, the Northern
Rockies and the Sierras, and heavy rain and flooding forecasts for Northern California.
I'm Louise Kivone, NPR News.

topics.text: EU negotiators deeply disappointed after Turkey climate talks collapse over omitted fossil fuel language
Leaked Pentagon memo limits military cooperation with Canada; Canadian defence minister says ties continue
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson condemns ICE arrest of two people boarding Seattle Alaska Airlines flight
Democrats reach at least 258 House seats after Chuck Hubbard defeats Virginia Fox in North Carolina
Researchers develop brain implant restoring singing ability for ALS patient, UC Davis neuroscientist Maitreyi Wairakar
Heavy rain forecast from Florida into New England, snow in Michigan and Rockies, flooding risk in Northern California
